name: Entner-Doudoroff Pathway (Semi-Phosphorylative)
notes: Semi-phosphorylative ED pathway: alternative glycolytic route found primarily in Gram-negative bacteria (Pseudomonas, E. coli) and some archaea. Converts glucose to glyceraldehyde-3P + pyruvate via phosphorylated intermediates and KDPG. Advantageous under aerobic, high-glucose conditions. Yields one ATP per glucose (vs two in EMP glycolysis) but generates NADPH for biosynthesis. Distinguished from EMP and pentose phosphate pathways by diagnostic enzymes edd and eda. Produces G3P which feeds into lower glycolysis.

nodes.name: glucokinase
nodes.notes: Phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6P; optional since G6P can be imported or derived from other pathways

nodes.name: glucose-6-phosphate 1-dehydrogenase
nodes.notes: Oxidizes G6P to 6-phosphoglucono-δ-lactone, generates NADPH; also participates in pentose phosphate pathway

nodes.name: 6-phosphogluconolactonase
nodes.notes: Alternative enzyme for lactonase step; also in pentose phosphate pathway

nodes.name: 6-phosphogluconolactonase
nodes.notes: Alternative lactonase; also in pentose phosphate pathway

nodes.name: phosphogluconate dehydratase
nodes.notes: Diagnostic enzyme unique to ED pathway; dehydrates 6-phosphogluconate to KDPG

nodes.name: 2-dehydro-3-deoxyphosphogluconate aldolase
nodes.notes: Diagnostic KDPG aldolase unique to ED pathway; cleaves KDPG to G3P and pyruvate

edges.notes: KDPG intermediate - diagnostic for ED pathway

scoring.notes: Core pathway (steps 2-5) required; upstream glucokinase optional. Diagnostic markers (edd/eda) distinguish ED from EMP and pentose phosphate pathways. At least one marker gene must be present for ED pathway identification.
